_about: College batch 5: junior year. COL_089, 073, 072, 075, 079, 084, 087, 098, 091, 092, 097, 074, 076 (chains: The Captain's Vote -> The Captain's Burden, The Integrity Hearing, Meeting the Family, When the Alum Gets Cut, The Agent's Dinner).

scenarios.title: The Big Deal
scenarios.text: A cash-advance app wants you as its face on campus: a season of posts, a billboard by the highway and the biggest NIL check on the team. The app charges students interest you'd never pay yourself, and you'd have to say you use it.

choices.label: Sign the deal
choices.result: You sign. The billboard goes up by the highway, the checks clear, and a few replies under your posts ask how you sleep at night.

choices.label: Ask for a product you'd use
choices.result: You tell them you'd only promote something you actually use. They pass, but a local sporting-goods store hears the story and offers a smaller deal you can sign with a straight face.

choices.label: Turn it down
choices.result: You say no and explain why to the teammate who set up the meeting. The money would have been nice, and you don't think about the billboard again.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Vote
scenarios.text: Captain voting is next week, and someone has written your name on the ballot. Kickers almost never get the votes, but a few teammates say this year could be different.

choices.label: Run for it
choices.result: You say yes and spend the week talking to every position group, not about you but about what the team needs. The vote is close, and when it's counted, you've got the patch.

choices.label: Back someone else
choices.result: You take your name off the ballot and tell the room to vote for the senior linebacker who has earned it. He wins, and he remembers who stood up for him.

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.result: You leave your name off and skip the speeches. You spend the extra hour in the film room every night that week instead.

choices.label: Ask {coach} first
choices.result: You've had a coach who trusted you completely, and you want that again. You ask {coach} what a captain from the specialists would need to do, then run on that answer and win.
choices.lock_text: having earned a coach's full confidence before

scenarios.title: The Runner
scenarios.text: A man in a nice jacket catches you in the parking lot after practice. He says he works 'with' an agent, hands you an envelope of cash and a new phone, and says there's more where that came from.

choices.label: Report him
choices.result: You hand the envelope back, take a photo of his license plate and walk straight to compliance. It's an awkward afternoon of forms, and your name never comes up in the story that follows.

choices.label: Hand it back and walk away
choices.result: You give it all back and say no thanks. He smiles like he'll try again, and you don't tell anyone.

choices.label: Keep the envelope
choices.result: You keep the cash and the phone. Three weeks later compliance calls you in: the runner's other players talked, and your name is on a list you can't explain.

scenarios.title: The Scouting Questionnaire
scenarios.text: A pro team sends you its first questionnaire: forty questions about your family, your habits and your goals. Question 14 asks you to describe any off-field incidents in your college career.

choices.label: Answer every question straight
choices.result: Whatever belongs on the page, you write it plainly, including the parts you'd rather forget, and ask {coach} to read it before you send it. It isn't all flattering, and it's all true.

choices.label: Shade a few answers
choices.result: You leave a couple of things out and soften the rest. It reads well. Whether it matches what the scouts already know is another question.

choices.label: Leave it for next year
choices.result: You put it in a drawer: it's a junior-year questionnaire, and you have midterms. The team's scout notes that you never sent it back.

choices.label: Add a page about what you stand for
choices.result: You answer the hard questions, then add a page about what you want from a pro career and what you won't do for one. A scout calls just to say nobody has ever sent that page before.
choices.lock_text: having been clear about what you wanted in recruiting

scenarios.title: The Mental Health Day
scenarios.text: You're tired in a way sleep doesn't fix. This morning you sat in the car outside the facility for twenty minutes before you could make yourself go in. The team counselor stops you in the hallway and says taking a day isn't weakness.

choices.label: Take the day
choices.result: You tell {coach} you need a day, and the coach just says okay. You sleep, call home and walk for an hour without your phone. The next morning, the drive in is just a drive.

choices.label: Push through it
choices.result: You go in anyway and get every rep. Nobody notices anything is wrong, which is the problem.

choices.label: Book a session with the counselor
choices.result: You don't take the day, but you take the counselor's Thursday slot. Talking it through doesn't fix the week. It does make it feel smaller.

scenarios.title: The Integrity Hearing
scenarios.text: Your professor has reported the paper. The hearing is next Tuesday: three faculty members, the paper on the table, and {teacher} in the chair beside you as your advisor.

choices.label: Admit it and accept the sanction
choices.result: You tell the panel exactly what happened before they ask. You get a zero on the paper and a semester of integrity workshops, and {teacher} says it's the first hearing in years where nobody had to drag the truth out.

choices.label: Ask {teacher} to speak for you
choices.result: You admit it, then ask {teacher} to tell the panel about the work you've done since. It doesn't erase anything, but the sanction comes back lighter.

choices.label: Say you didn't know it was cheating
choices.result: You argue the tutor only 'edited' it. The panel doesn't buy it, the sanction doubles, and the coaches hear about it before you're back at the facility.

scenarios.title: The Twenty-First Birthday
scenarios.text: A teammate turns twenty-one on a Thursday, and the whole position room is going out to celebrate. Practice is at seven the next morning.

choices.label: Be the driver
choices.result: You come along as the driver, order wings and water, and have everyone home by midnight. At seven you're the only one in the room who looks awake, and the birthday boy texts you a thank-you at noon.

choices.label: Buy him dinner, then go home
choices.result: You take him to dinner early, give a toast and head home at nine. He's a little disappointed, and you're asleep before the night gets loud.

choices.label: Stay out until close
choices.result: You stay out until the lights come on and walk into practice at 7:04 in sunglasses. {coach} sends you home, and the whole team watches you go.

scenarios.title: Hosting a Recruit
scenarios.text: A high school kicker is on his official visit this weekend, and {coach} has asked you to host. On the first night, the recruit leans over and says he wants to see 'the real college experience,' and two teammates already have a party planned.

choices.label: Show him the real thing
choices.result: You take him to the team dinner, the film room and the late-night pancake place every player swears by, and you tell him the truth about the hard weeks. He commits a month later and asks for you by name.

choices.label: Keep it short and safe
choices.result: You give him the campus tour, have him back at the hotel by ten and call it a night. He's polite about it. He also doesn't commit.

choices.label: Take him to the party
choices.result: You take him to the party and lose track of him around midnight. His parents call {coach} the next morning, and the recruit commits somewhere else.

choices.label: Tell him what you wish you'd heard
choices.result: You skip the party, buy him a burger and tell him how you handled your own recruiting: be honest with every coach, early. He asks a hundred questions, and {coach} hears about it from the recruit's dad.
choices.lock_text: having been honest with every coach in your own recruiting

scenarios.title: The Ultimatum
scenarios.text: You and {love_interest} have made the long distance work for two years of bus tickets and late calls. Now they want next summer, all of it, at home instead of at the summer program on campus. 'For once,' they say, 'pick us.'

choices.label: Spend the summer at home
choices.result: You tell {coach} you'll train at home and send film every week. The coach isn't thrilled. {love_interest} cries on the phone, the good kind.

choices.label: Stay for the summer program
choices.result: You explain why the program matters and promise to visit every other weekend. {love_interest} says they understand, and the call ends quieter than it started.

choices.label: Split the summer
choices.result: You'll spend half the summer at home and half on campus. Nobody gets everything, there's a lot of driving, and you both feel heard.

scenarios.title: Meeting the Family
scenarios.text: The person you're dating wants you to meet their family over the long holiday weekend: four days, their parents and their grandmother's cooking. It's the same weekend as the team's leadership retreat.

choices.label: Go meet the family
choices.result: You skip the retreat, drive six hours and spend four days answering questions about kicking from people who have never watched football. On the drive home, you're both quiet and happy.

choices.label: Go to the retreat
choices.result: You go to the retreat and promise to meet the family at the next break. It's the right call for the team, and you spend more of the weekend on your phone than you'd like.

choices.label: Leave the retreat a day early
choices.result: You ask {coach} to let you miss the last day and drive to the family's house for Sunday dinner. It's short, and it's enough to start.

scenarios.title: When the Alum Gets Cut
scenarios.text: The pro kicker who trained you two summers ago gets cut on a Tuesday. He calls you that night, before he has told almost anyone, and he sounds like a different person.

choices.label: Just listen
choices.result: You let him talk for an hour about the tryouts, the waiver wire and what he'll tell his kids. He thanks you for not trying to fix it.

choices.label: Ask what he'd do differently
choices.result: Once he's calmer, you ask what he'd change if he were twenty-one again. You fill three pages, and half of it isn't about kicking.

choices.label: Go straight to the net
choices.result: You hang up and go to the net under the lights. If it can happen to him, it can happen to you.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Burden
scenarios.text: A starting linebacker missed curfew on a road trip, and the coaches don't know yet. He finds you in the hotel hallway and asks you, as one of the team's leaders, to keep it in the locker room.

choices.label: Give him until breakfast
choices.result: You tell him he has until breakfast to tell {coach} himself, or you will. He tells. He's furious for a week, and then he starts showing up early.

choices.label: Handle it player to player
choices.result: You make him run the stadium stairs with you at six the next morning and leave the coaches out of it. The room respects it, and the coaches never hear a thing.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.result: You tell him not to let it happen again and leave it there. It doesn't come up again, but two younger players saw the whole thing.

scenarios.title: The Agent's Dinner
scenarios.text: An agent you've never met invites you to the best steakhouse in town to 'talk about your future,' and he's picking up the check. It's a year before you're allowed to sign with anyone, and you both know the rules.

choices.label: Decline and wait
choices.result: You thank him, say you'll talk after your last game like the rules say, and mention the invitation to {coach}. He says he respects that. He also says the offer won't be this good next year.

choices.label: Go to dinner, sign nothing
choices.result: You eat the steak, listen to the pitch and leave without signing anything. It's within the rules, barely, and his texts start arriving every week after.

choices.label: Shake on a secret deal
choices.result: He slides an envelope across the table, a 'loan' against your future, and you shake on a deal nobody can know about. You spend the summer checking your phone for a compliance email.
